title.narrative: Girls Empowerment and Quality Education for All Project

description.narrative: The Girls Empowerment and Quality Education for All (P169222) would be financed through a proposed IDA grant in the amount of US$15 million and a proposed GPE grant in the amount of US$2.2 million, using an Investment Project Financing (IPF) lending instrument. The Project aims to address the challenges of supporting a more conducive learning environment for girls empowerment, system-wide activities to tackle the learning poverty and reaching the most vulnerable. The scope of the Project is general education (covering preschool throughout secondary education), but each component would focus on different levels of education to achieve the development objectives.
The Project Development Objective are to equip girls with life skills and improve student learning outcomes for all.

title.narrative: Girls improving life skills under the project

comment.narrative: Progress under Subcomponent 1.1 is monitored through pre- and post-assessments of beneficiaries life skills, with a focus on competencies that raise aspirations and strengthen agency among girls, including financial literacy, sexual and reproductive health knowledge, and self-confidence. Result is shown as the weighted average for 2023/24 and 2024/25 school years. Gains in aspiration-related dimensions appear more modest, reflecting the country's challenging economic context, characterized by limited job creation, weak labor market prospects, and high youth emigration, which may dampen expectations about future opportunities despite continued improvements in knowledge, agency, and socio-emotional skills.

title.narrative: Teachers trained under the project who demonstrated improved teaching practices in the classroom

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the share of teachers trained in literacy and numeracy under the project who demonstrate improved classroom teaching practices, as assessed through classroom observations using the TEACH instrument. Between the TEACH assessments conducted in 2022 and 2024, the proportion of trained teachers scoring above the benchmark average of 3 points increased from 10.15 percent (baseline) to 51.9 percent (actual), representing an increase of 41.75 percentage points.

title.narrative: Teachers trained in literacy and numeracy through structured training

comment.narrative: The ratio between the number of teachers of basic education schools trained in literacy and numeracy through structured training under the project, and the total number of teachers in basic education schools. The hiring of a firm to develop the structured materials and conduct the training of basic education teachers is ongoing.

title.narrative: Preschool teachers receiving in-service training under the project

comment.narrative: The indicator measures the ratio of preschool teachers receiving in-service training under the project to the total number of preschool teachers in the system. The system included 1,051 preschool teachers and pedagogical assistants. Under the project, 575 professionals were trained during the first phase and 538 during the second phase, resulting in a total of 1,113 teachers and pedagogical assistants trained. This exceeds the initial number of professionals recorded in the system, indicating that training coverage reached 100 percent and included additional personnel (e.g., newly recruited or replacement staff).

title.narrative: Basic and secondary schools participating in the WASH Program

comment.narrative: WASH interventions have been completed in nine schools. Rehabilitation works in an additional four schools are ongoing and expected to be completed by May 2026. Rehabilitation in two additional schools is scheduled to commence in March 2026, while procurement of works for the remaining two schools is underway.

Percentage of girls who participared in the boys' and girls' clubs with career aspirations to start tertiary education after graduating from secondary education. Results is shown as the weighted average for 2023/24 and 2024/25 school years.

title.narrative: Revise and adopt MEES Human Resources Policy

comment.narrative: This activity supports the revision and adoption of MECC's Human Resources Policy, including recruitment, deployment, career progression, and retirement. The technical assistance to review MECC's human resources policy has been completed, and the focus has now shifted to policy implementation.
This indicator refers to preschool teachers who received in-service training and basic education teachers trained in literacy and numeracy through structured training under the project.

title.narrative: Ministry staff trained in Inclusive Education

comment.narrative: Number of ministry staff trained in Inclusive Education. The process to hire the firm that will review the special education strategy and conduct the training of Ministry staff in inclusive education is ongoing.

title.narrative: Number of grievances received and addressed through the project the GRM system

comment.narrative: Since the introduction of the registration system, 27 disciplinary cases have been recorded, all of which have now been concluded. The most severe sanction provided for by law—dismissal—was applied, demonstrating the Ministry's commitment to accountability and enforcement of disciplinary measures.

title.narrative: Large-scale learning assessments completed at the primary or secondary levels

comment.narrative: Number of national learning assessments (AALEB and AALES) and international learning assessment (PASEC) completed. PASEC will be considered completed when reports are received and results disseminated.

title.narrative: Students benefiting from direct interventions to enhance learning

comment.narrative: Students participating in PASEC, ALLEB, and ALLES are all considered as beneficiaries of activities to enhance learning.

title.narrative: Grade 2 students who have improved grade-level competencies in numeracy

comment.narrative: Percentage of grade 2 students who have grade-level competencies in numeracy in the PASEC student assessment. Baseline data is the round of PASEC applied in 2022 (53.70 percent). The second round of PASEC was conducted in May 2025. Data to be reported when new PASEC results become available.

title.narrative: Carry out PASEC, analyze results and disseminate findings

comment.narrative: PASEC was carried out in 2022 for students in 2nd and 6th grades. The PASEC 2022 report was published and results have been disseminated to the school community. A new round of PASEC was carried out in May 2025 for students in 2nd, 6th and 9th grades. Data is being decoded and the final report is expected by April 2026.

title.narrative: Completion rate in secondary education (disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative: According to the 2022/23 education statistical bulletin, completion rates for students in secondary education increased to 57 percent compared to 51 percent in the previous school calendar year. However, progress toward the secondary education completion rate indicator has reversed, with a sharp decline observed during the reporting period. This trend coincides with rising youth emigration, which has reduced retention at the secondary level as migration has increasingly become a perceived alternative pathway to employment.

title.narrative: Schools with infrastructure adapted to children living with disabilities

comment.narrative: Schools that are being retrofitted through rehabilitations such that they are made more accessible for children living with disabilities. This is especially true for the bathrooms.

title.narrative: Number of schools benefiting from girl-friendly programming

comment.narrative: Number of schools that are benefiting from behavior change communication activities, including menstrual health management. Behavior change content has been developed and menstrual health management materials were purchased.

title.narrative: Number of children participating in girls' and boys' clubs

comment.narrative: Number of girls and boys registered as members of the girls' and boys' clubs, for school years 2023/24 and 2024/25.

title.narrative: Grade 2 students who have improved grade-level competencies in literacy

comment.narrative: Percentage of grade 2 students who have grade-level competencies in literacy in the PASEC student assessment. Baseline data is the round of PASEC applied in 2022 (56.60 percent). The second round of PASEC was conducted in May 2025. Data to be reported when new PASEC results become available.
